question.prompt: The acute angles of a right triangle are \(a^{\circ}\) and \(b^{\circ},\) where \(a>b\) and both \(a\) and \(b\) are prime numbers. What is the least possible value of \(b?\)

solutions.title: Test the smallest primes
solutions.explanation:
The acute angles of a right triangle add to \(90^\circ\), so choosing \(b\) determines \(a=90-b\).

Test prime values of \(b\) in increasing order:
\[
\begin{aligned}
b=2&\implies a=88=2\cdot44,\\
b=3&\implies a=87=3\cdot29,\\
b=5&\implies a=85=5\cdot17.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each of these makes \(a\) composite. The next prime is \(7\), which gives \(a=83\).

To check that \(83\) is prime, only the primes \(2,3,5,7\) need testing. A composite number has a prime factor no larger than its square root, and \(\sqrt{83}<10\). None of these four primes divides \(83\).

The angles \(83^\circ\) and \(7^\circ\) are acute and satisfy \(a>b\). Since every smaller prime value of \(b\) failed, the least possible value is \(\boxed{7}\), choice \(\textbf{D}\).

solutions.title: Use divisibility
solutions.explanation:
Because \(a\) and \(b\) are different primes, \(b\) cannot divide \(a\). This lets us rule out several small values of \(b\) together.

The right triangle gives \(a+b=90\). If \(b\) divided \(90\), it would also divide \(90-b=a\). Since \(a\) is prime and \(b>1\), that would force \(a=b\), contradicting \(a>b\).

Thus \(b\) cannot be any of \(2,3,5\), since each divides \(90\). The smallest remaining prime is \(7\). Taking \(b=7\) gives \(a=83\).

The number \(83\) is prime: any composite number has a prime factor at most its square root, but none of the primes \(2,3,5,7\) below \(\sqrt{83}<10\) divides it. Both angles are acute, and \(83>7\).

Therefore the least possible value is \(\boxed{7}\), choice \(\textbf{D}\).
